title: Skin-to-Skin Contact Start Time in Newborns Sucking and Mother's Breastfeeding Willingness and Parent-Infant Attachment Associated
brief_summary: The maternal and child skin contact in the early postpartum period, so that the newborn can show effective sucking ability, will affect the self-confidence of the mother's feeding, and is also one of the factors affecting the mother's exclusive breastfeeding. The purpose of this study was to discuss the relationship between the onset of maternal and child skin contact and the relationship between neonatal milk, mother's willingness to breastfeed and parent-child attachment.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* 37 weeks to 40 weeks of gestation
* No high risk pregnancy
* No nipple abnormality
* Willing to breastfeed
* Newborn weight 2500-4000 grams

Exclusion Criteria:

* High risk pregnancy
* 37 weeks ago
* Major bleeding during production
* Neonatal life signs abnormality
* Neonatal oral structure abnormalities
